answer: Costly work receipts. Every new identity must complete useful, verified work whose reward is released only after a delay, so a clone's payoff sinks toward the nadir until real demand arrives. During that delay, a random subset of peers checks the work under a lantern of public audit, and failed checks forfeit the accrued reward. The tide of competing identities dilutes each reward share while audit labor cost stays fixed, making every extra clone strictly negative-EV before it earns anything.
